message.reasoning_content:
Record the _append indexing claim (in_scope) and a second claim about order composition / appended after reorder. Let me verify indexing logic.

Convention: physical slot p holds logical row i where order[i]=p. After reorder op: logical row i = old logical row P[i], so new_order[i] = old_order[P[i]]. ✓ _reorder correct.

Append: logical row i should get Delta[i]. Logical row i lives at physical order[i], so physical slot order[i] should receive Delta[i]. Kernel: physical slot `row` receives Delta[order[row]]. Setting p=row: kernel adds Delta[order⁻¹(p)]... wait order[row] where row is the physical slot p — so physical slot p gets Delta[order[p]], correct is Delta[order⁻¹[p]]. Equivalent only if order is involution. Confirmed suspicion. Words like (0,1,2) with non-involution composition fail — unless P0∘P1 happens to be an involution for this seed; need runtime evidence, but claim stands as testable.
